summary: Shoji Mori, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his BA and studied further at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi. He held posts as an assistant professor and professor at Toyo University and was a researcher at Okurayama Institute.
A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Shoju Inaba served as a professor at Otani University, attested in 1962, and as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.
Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Ueno Gakuen University and Otani University.

Shokin Furuta was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Matsue High School, Shimane University, the University of Tokyo under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, and Tokyo University of Education, later serving as professor at Hokkaido and Nihon universities.
A scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies, Shoko Kanaoka held academic positions at Toyo University, where he is attested as a professor in 1987 and present in 2000.

Shoko Miyabayashi specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, completing his undergraduate and master's studies at Taisho University. He later served there as lecturer in 1960, assistant professor in 1962, and Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies from 1978 to 2002.

Shoko Miyata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Miyata has served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, attested in 2026.
Shoko Takeuchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later became a professor emeritus at Ryukoku University, attested from 1987 to 1995.

Shoko Watanabe studied under Naoshiro Tsuji and Ernst Leumann at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Toyo University. His posts included professor at Taisho University and Toyo University, as well as positions at Kyushu and Tokyo universities.

Shoku Bando studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg. In 1987, he held appointments at the Abhidharma Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoryu Katsura studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto. A specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he was Professor Emeritus at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Professor at Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shoshin Fukihara studied at Otani University under Susumu Yamaguchi and at Horyuji Kangakuin under Join Saeki. He held posts at Otani University, Doho University, Otani Senshu Gakuin, and Otani University Junior College.

Shoshin Ichishima is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and held appointments at Taisho University, including Dean of Academic Affairs and Professor Emeritus.

Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of archaeology, history, and Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from 1957 to 1966, subsequently serving there as assistant professor and Professor Emeritus at the Institute for Research in Humanities.

Shoshun Hayashidera specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Hayashidera was affiliated with the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, attested in 2011, and is attested as a professor at Hokkaido University in 2026.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Shoson Miyamoto studied at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa University, Waseda University, and Toyo University.

Shou-chien Shih is a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He served as a professor at National Taiwan University from 1984 to 2006 and was the director of the National Palace Museum from approximately 2004 to 2006.

Shozen Kumoi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner in Vienna. He served as assistant professor at Otani University (1948–1981) and as professor at Bukkyo University in 1982.
Shri Krishna Saksena was a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Lucknow and as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Shri Krishna Sharma was an Indologist and linguist. He founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.
